mainTopic: Can two partial actions join into one? אילפא's question about washing a hand in halves, parallel questions from רבי ירמיה and רב פפא, and a return to the משנה about two agents bringing a גט.
overview: The גמרא keeps working on אילפא's question: if someone washes half his hand and then the other half, do the two washings join? It first quotes a משנה that plain moisture (משקה טופח) is not a חיבור, which seems to settle it. The answer is that the question is about a hand wet enough to wet something else (טופח להטפיח). The גמרא objects that we already know such wetness is a חיבור. It replies that this rule may apply only to a מקוה and only according to רבי יהודה. It then quotes his view in the משנה about two people immersing in a מקוה of exactly forty סאה. Next, רבי ירמיה and רב פפא each ask a similar question about joining two different methods halfway: entering drawn water plus having it fall on you, and immersing plus having water poured on you. Both questions end in תיקו. Finally the גמרא returns to our משנה about one agent who saw the גט written and one who saw it signed. רבי יוחנן begins to limit that ruling, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Plain moisture does not connect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a pouring stream, water running down a slope, and plain moisture are not a חיבור, either for טומאה or for טהרה. This seems to answer אילפא's question: the wet half of the hand should not join with the second washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pouring stream, water running down a slope, and liquid that is only moist do not count as a connection, not for impurity and not for purity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אילפא's question by quoting a משנה. The משנה says that just moisture does not connect two bodies of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אילפא asked whether washing half the hand and then the other half works. The water left on the first half is only moisture, and the משנה says moisture is never a חיבור. If so, the answer seems obvious, and the question looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A stream of liquid being poured from one vessel into another
A slope; water flowing down an incline
Liquid that is only moist, a thin wetness
A connection that makes two bodies of water count as one
For passing on impurity, or for joining water into an amount that can purify

phrases.english: A pouring stream, and water running down a slope,
and liquid that is only moist —
are not a connection
neither for impurity nor for purity!
phrases.notes: So the moist half of the hand should not join with the water of the second washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of אילפא's question from before this section by bringing a משנה against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: אילפא's question about washing the hand in two halves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Moisture is not a חיבור, so the answer is obvious and the question is unnecessary.

steps.title: The question is about a hand that is very wet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אילפא's question is about a hand wet enough to make something else wet (טופח להטפיח), not just slightly moist.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed where the wetness is enough to make something else wet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אילפא's question by narrowing the case. The washed half of the hand is wet enough to wet something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only spoke about thin moisture. Thicker wetness that can pass on to something else might count as a חיבור, so the question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a specific case)
Wet enough to make something else wet

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where there is wetness enough to make something else wet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about any moisture, which the משנה already says is not a חיבור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about wetness that can wet something else, which the משנה did not cover.

steps.title: We already learned that strong wetness connects
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a ruling already exists: wetness that can wet something else (טופח להטפיח) is a חיבור. If so, אילפא's question is already answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this too: wetness enough to make something else wet is a connection!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new version of the question. A known ruling already says that this kind of wetness counts as a חיבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 saved the question by talking about strong wetness. But if a source already says strong wetness connects, the answer is known, so אילפא would have no reason to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned this too

phrases.english: We already learned this too:
wetness enough to make something else wet is a connection!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The narrowed version of אילפא's question from step 2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known source already rules that טופח להטפיח is a חיבור, so the question has no reason to exist.

steps.title: That rule may be only about a מקוה, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the rule 'טופח להטפיח is a חיבור' may apply only to a מקוה, and may follow only the view of רבי יהודה. So אילפא could still ask about washing hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that rule was said about מקואות, and it follows the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אילפא's question again. It suggests the earlier rule is limited: it applies only to a מקוה and only according to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule comes from the laws of a מקוה, we cannot be sure it applies to washing hands (נטילת ידים). If it is only רבי יהודה's view, other תנאים may disagree. Either way, אילפא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
Regarding the laws of ritual baths

phrases.english: Perhaps that was said about ritual baths,
and it follows the view of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא לְעִנְיַן מִקְוָאוֹת, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by limiting the source it relied on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to one topic and one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule 'טופח להטפיח is a חיבור' is general and also settles the hand-washing question.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule may apply only to a מקוה and only per רבי יהודה, so the hand-washing question is still open.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the rule is wrong. It only says the rule may be limited to a מקוה and to one תנא, so it cannot settle אילפא's question.

steps.title: The משנה of two people immersing in a forty-סאה מקוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting the משנה where רבי יהודה's view appears. In a מקוה of exactly forty סאה, if two people immerse at the same time, both are pure. If they immerse one after the other, the first is pure and the second is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a מקוה that has exactly forty סאה, and two people went down and immersed: if both immersed at once, they are pure. If one after the other, the first is pure and the second is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind step 4: a משנה about a מקוה that has exactly the minimum amount of water. This sets up רבי יהודה's view, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the first person climbs out, some water clings to his body, so the מקוה now has a little less than forty סאה. That is why the second person stays impure. This sets the stage for רבי יהודה, who will treat the water on the first person as connected to the מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a kosher מקוה
Exactly, not a drop more
At the same time
One after the other

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
A ritual bath that has in it
exactly forty se'ah,
and two people went down and immersed
(if both at the same time, they are pure),
phrases.notes: Some versions of the גמרא leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: if one after the other —
the first is pure, and the second is impure.
phrases.notes: Water clung to the first person as he came out, so less than forty סאה was left for the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מְכוּוָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה that stands behind the suggestion in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the rule about טופח להטפיח comes from the laws of a מקוה and follows רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מקואות about two people immersing in a מקוה of exactly forty סאה
steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows how water clinging to a person can affect whether a מקוה still counts. רבי יהודה's view on this case, coming next, is the source for the idea that strong wetness is a חיבור.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the second person is also pure if the first one's feet still touch the water
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה ends with רבי יהודה's view. If the first person's feet are still in the water, the second person is pure too. This shows that for him, water still connected to a body joins with the מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if the first person's feet were still touching the water, the second person is also pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it began in step 5 and reaches רבי יהודה's opinion, which is the whole reason it quoted this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said the second person is impure, because the first person took some water out with him and now the מקוה is under forty סאה. רבי יהודה says that as long as the first person's feet touch the water, the water on his body still counts as part of the מקוה. So for רבי יהודה, wet water that can wet something else (טופח להטפיח) joins, but this is only shown for a מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: his feet
touching the water
ritually pure
the first person / the second person

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'טופח להטפיח is a חיבור' comes from רבי יהודה and is said about a מקוה. That is why אילפא could still ask about washing hands.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never says the word 'טופח להטפיח'. The גמרא learns it from the reason רבי יהודה makes the second person pure: the water on the first person's body still joins the מקוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the answer from step 4. The source for 'טופח להטפיח is a חיבור' is limited to a מקוה and to רבי יהודה, so אילפא's question about hands is still open.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If the feet of the first one were
touching the water,
phrases.notes: He means the first person stepped out but his feet were still in the מקוה when the second person immersed.

phrases.english: then the second one is also pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיוּ רַגְלָיו שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן נוֹגְעוֹת בַּמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote from step 5 and gives the actual source for the claim in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'טופח להטפיח is a חיבור' is only רבי יהודה's view, and only about a מקוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה in the משנה about two people immersing in a forty-סאה מקוה (מקואות)

steps.title: רבי ירמיה cites a known rule about drawn water making a person impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה cites a known rule with two cases. In both, drawn water makes a pure person impure: when he enters it with his head and most of his body, or when three לוגין of it fall on his head and most of his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: They have taught that if someone puts his head and most of his body into drawn water, or if three לוגין of drawn water fall on the head and most of the body of a pure person, he becomes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another question similar to אילפא's. Here רבי ירמיה is only setting up the base rule that his question in the next step will build on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate ways drawn water can make a pure person impure. One is going into it (ביאה). The other is having it fall on him (נפילה). In both, it has to reach the head and most of the body.

keyTerms.meaning: drawn water, water collected by people in a vessel, not natural water
his head and most of his body
a small liquid measure / measures
'they have said', introducing an earlier ruling

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: They have said:
One who enters with his head and most of his body
into drawn water,

phrases.aramaic: וְטָהוֹר שֶׁנָּפְלוּ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ וְעַל רוּבּוֹ
phrases.english: and a pure person on whose head and most of his body there fell
three לוגין of drawn water,
is impure.
phrases.notes: This one word covers both cases: the person who went in and the person the water fell on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel question about joining two partial actions, similar to אילפא's question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawn water makes a pure person impure, either by entering it with head and most of the body, or by three לוגין falling on head and most of the body.

steps.title: Half by entering and half by falling: do they combine?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about half the body going into drawn water and the other half having drawn water fall on it. Do the two halves join to make the person impure? The question is left unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: if half of him got wet by entering and half by water falling on him, what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks whether the two methods from the rule he just cited can join together. The גמרא has no answer and says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each method needs the head and most of the body. Here neither method alone covers that much, but together they do. This is the same kind of question as אילפא's: can two different partial actions join into one full action?

keyTerms.meaning: he asked (a real question of law)
entering into the water
water falling onto the person
'let it stand', the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
Half of him by entering and half of him by falling — what is the law?
Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: חֶצְיוֹ בְּבִיאָה וְחֶצְיוֹ בִּנְפִילָה, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the two methods described in step 7 can combine.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether half the body by entering and half by falling join together to make the person impure.

steps.title: רב פפא cites the rule that pouring nine קבין purifies a sick בעל קרי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא cites a known rule. A sick בעל קרי becomes pure when nine קבין of water are poured on him; he does not need to immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They have taught that a sick בעל קרי who had nine קבין of water poured on him is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third question of the same kind. רב פפא first sets up the base rule his question will build on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בעל קרי purifies himself by immersing in a מקוה (טבילה). For a sick person there is an easier way: pouring nine קבין of water on him (נתינה). So again there are two separate ways to reach the same result.

keyTerms.meaning: a man who had a seminal emission
sick
nine קבין, a measure of water

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: They have said:
a sick man who had a seminal emission,
on whom they poured nine קבין of water,
is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel case about joining two methods, after אילפא's and רבי ירמיה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick בעל קרי is purified by having nine קבין of water poured on him.

steps.title: Half by immersion and half by pouring: do they combine?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about half the body being immersed and the other half having water poured on it. Is the person pure? The question is left unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: if half of him was immersed and half had water poured on it, what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks whether טבילה and נתינה can join to purify the whole person. Again the גמרא says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each method on its own purifies the whole body. The question is whether one half done each way counts as one complete purification. It ends unresolved, just like רבי ירמיה's question.

keyTerms.meaning: immersion in a מקוה
pouring water onto the person

steps.whatToRemember: There are three similar questions about joining two partial actions: אילפא's (washing hands), רבי ירמיה's (entering plus falling), and רב פפא's (immersing plus pouring). The last two both end in תיקו.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
Half of him by immersion and half of him by pouring — what is the law?
Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: חֶצְיוֹ בִּטְבִילָה וְחֶצְיוֹ בִּנְתִינָה, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the method in step 9 can combine with regular immersion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether half by immersion and half by pouring join together to purify the person.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the ruling about one witness to writing and one to signing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to our משנה. One agent says 'it was written in front of me' and the other says 'it was signed in front of me.' רבי יוחנן says the משנה's ruling only applies when the גט did not come from both of them. He then begins to say what happens when it did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: one says 'It was written in my presence' and one says, etc. רב שמואל בר יהודה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They only taught this when the גט does not come out from the hands of both of them. But when the גט comes out from the hands of both of them...
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about bringing a גט, and רבי יוחנן starts to limit it. His statement is not finished yet and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says this גט is invalid. רבי יוחנן says that is only when the גט is not handed over by both men together. In that case only one of them is the agent, and he did not say the full statement himself. The case where both of them bring the גט is about to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it was written in my presence', a statement the agent must make
'they only taught this when...', limiting a ruling
a bill of divorce
comes out from the hands of both of them, meaning both are bringing it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's sentence is cut off here. The ruling for when both men bring the גט comes on the next amud, so don't guess it yet.

phrases.english: One says: "It was written in my presence,"
and one says, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the rest of the line in the משנה: the other says it was signed in front of him, and the גט is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught this only

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין הַגֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: where the גט does not come out from the hands of both of them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל גֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם –
phrases.english: but a גט that comes out from the hands of both of them —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to our משנה after the side discussion about joining partial actions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's ruling that the גט is invalid applies only when the גט is not brought by both men together. The other case is about to be explained.
